highlight.text: Goya's usage of the recently developed technique of aquatint (etching a printing plate so that tones similar to watercolor washes can be reproduced) gave Los Caprichos pronounced tonal effects and spirited contrast that made them a major achievement in the history of engraving.

work.text: Created between 1797 and 1799 for the Diario de Madrid, it is the 43rd of the 80 aquatints making up the satirical Los caprichos.

source.author: Wikipedia contributors
source.title: The Sleep of Reason Produces Monsters

work.text: Many observers believe that Goya intended to depict himself asleep amidst his drawing tools, his reason dulled by slumber, bedeviled by creatures that prowl in the dark.

source.author: Wikipedia contributors
source.title: The Sleep of Reason Produces Monsters

moment.text: Los Caprichos is a series of 80 etchings published in 1799 wherein Goya criticized the rampant political, social, and religious abuses of the time period.

source.author: Wikipedia contributors
source.title: The Sleep of Reason Produces Monsters

matters.text: Imagination abandoned by reason produces impossible monsters; united with her, she is the mother of the arts and source of their wonders

source.author: Francisco Goya
